messages:
carla: @channel heads up — right after the 08:30 canary deploy p95 jumped from ~420ms to 2.5s, p99 to ~6.2s. We're seeing a surge of 504s on /v1/generate and gateway timeouts. Pager fired. :rotating_light:
ben: seeing the same in dashboards. errors are 502/504 and a small bump in internal 5xx from conv-runtime. TG for oncall.
alice: I grabbed logs — conv-runtime has a backlog on the multiplexer and a lot of 'write timeout to kvcache' warnings. Not a full OOM but connection churn to kvcache hosts.
observability-bot: Alert: service=frontend endpoint=/v1/generate p95=2500ms p99=6200ms 5xx_rate=7.8% region=us-west-2
sam: Can we confirm this is correlated with the new runtime change? Which revision went live in canary?
carla: canary hash 3f9b2a -> promoted 08:30. The change was multiplexing concurrency adjustments + ephemeral conn pooling tweak.
ben: immediate ask — roll the canary back to previous revision for the gateway/runtime. If rollback path is quick we should do it.
alice: preparing rollback. running: ```kubectl -n runtime rollout undo deployment/conv-runtime --to-revision=42``` and ```kubectl -n gateway rollout undo deployment/gateway --to-revision=37```
incident-bot: Pager duty: oncall sam acknowledged the incident. Response stage: mitigations in progress.
sam: while rollback runs, enable fallback-routing to stable model pool and reduce mux concurrency to avoid head-of-line blocking. I'll flip the route in the router: ```routerctl route set /v1/generate backend=stable-variant-1 weight=90```
carla: customer impact — only public hosted API traffic, mostly US-West. No Dedicated customers reported errors yet via support, but spike in user error reports. estimate: ~3% of requests failing, some higher-traffic customers seeing tail latency spikes.
ben: logs from gateway showing repeated "connection reset by peer" to kvcache nodes and stack traces with kvclient timeouts. Might be a kvcache connection limit regression introduced by the pooling change.
alice: kvcache hosts show increased ephemeral connections; connection count > expected. I'm adding a short-term limit: ```kv-config set max_ephemeral_conn=250``` and restarting the kv-proxy with graceful drain.
observability-bot: Metric update (08:40): p95=1.8s p99=4.5s 5xx_rate=5.2% after initial rollbacks started. Some improvement but still above SLO.
sam: rollback of conv-runtime completed 08:42 — gateway still rolling. Rolling traffic back to stable, watching traces.
carla: confirming customer-facing errors dropping on our synthetics. Switching to monitoring-only channel. Any need for broader comms? Support triage is ready if we hit customers with higher impact.
ben: I'll keep paging active for 30m and then hand off. Remaining items: postmortem, root cause — suspected kvcache pooling regression; need to repro on staging. Also check whether connection keepalive defaults changed.
alice: capturing logs and reproducer steps. I'll snapshot kvcache proxies and configs and create a runbook entry for future fast rollback of pooling flags.
eve: (next oncall) I'm taking handoff at 09:00. Current status: p95 back to ~480ms, p99 ~760ms, 5xx_rate ~0.6%. Please DM me the rollback commands and links to traces.
carla: sending links: https://dashboards/redwood/alerts/1762223333 and traces: https://traces/redwood/trace/3f9b2a. Also adding PR refs and diff for the pooling change.
sam: closing pager in 20 min if metrics stay stable; assign postmortem to infra and runtime teams. Marking incident SEV-2. :white_check_mark:
carla: thanks all — logging timeline and notes in incident channel. follow-up tasks: postmortem, test for kvcache conn saturation, add circuit-breaker in mux to protect head requests.
incident-bot: Incident update: status=mitigated severity=SEV-2 owner=sam followup=infrastructure-runtime postmortem=true
eve: acknowledged handoff. I'll keep an eye on anomalies and message if anything regresses.
carla: thanks — end of thread.
